svg.title: Firewalls: stateless filtering vs stateful connection tracking
svg.desc: A stateful firewall remembers outbound conversations, so replies are allowed automatically and unsolicited traffic is not
svg.text: Firewalls: stateless filtering vs stateful connection tracking
A stateful firewall remembers outbound conversations, so replies are allowed automatically and unsolicited traffic is not
STATELESS · classic ACL · judges every packet alone
2 permit tcp any eq 443 → inside (reply rule, risky)
unsolicited SYN from outside → no entry → DROP
SECURITY ZONES · POLICY IS WRITTEN PER DIRECTION
Reading: row = where traffic starts, column = where it is going. Anything not listed is denied.
Stateful = a table of established connections. Reply traffic is allowed because the firewall remembers the request.
Default posture: deny everything crossing zones, then permit only what each application genuinely needs.
